title: Resolving discs and mergers in z ∼ 2 heavily reddened quasars and their companion galaxies with ALMA
question: How are major physical processes governing massive galaxy formation (mergers, starbursts, black-hole growth, outflows) triggered during the dust-obscured quasar phase, and what effect do they have on the quasar host galaxies?

data.sensitivity: Line (15.625 MHz channels): 0.10 mJy beam^-1 (J1234), 0.14 mJy beam^-1 (J2315); Continuum: 11.5 uJy beam^-1 (J1234), 9.3 uJy beam^-1 (J2315)

what.value: CO(1-0), CO(7-6), CI(2-1) line profiles and gas masses for the J1234 and J2315 systems

evidence.quote: In (cite: Banerji:18) (Paper I hereafter) we combined the CO(3-2) detections with detections of CO(1-0), CO(7-6) and CI(2-1) to better constrain the interstellar medium properties of the quasar host galaxies.

In Paper I, we derived gas masses for all galaxies in the J1234 system using several different estimators, thus mitigating against the uncertainties implicit in using a single molecular tracer of the total gas mass.

recipe.goal: Extract 1D spectra, create moment maps, and measure source sizes and line/continuum properties
recipe.method: Identify 3D signal mask using 3DBarolo SEARCH utility, collapse significant line channels into moment 0, 1, and 2 maps using CASA immoments, fit 2D Gaussians to moment 0 maps with CASA imfit and in the uv-plane with uvmodelfit, extract spectra in 1-2'' apertures, and fit 1D Gaussian components to spectral line profiles.
key_parameters: Aperture diameter 1-2''; SEARCH thresholds S/N_upper = 3.5 and S/N_lower = 3.0
assumptions: r_1/2 = 0.5 x FWHM for a Gaussian profile

recipe.goal: Model 3D gas kinematics and derive inner dynamical masses using tilted-ring fitting
recipe.method: Fit 3D tilted-ring models directly to the CO(3-2) data cubes using 3DBarolo, convolving models with the restoring beam channel-by-channel, and compute dynamical mass from M_dyn = v_rot,max^2 * r_max / G.
key_parameters: 3 rings; max model radius = 1.0 x deconvolved major axis FWHM; min ring width = (beam minor axis FWHM)/2.5; initial inclination = 45 deg (allowed range 10-80 deg); scale height Z_o = 0.01'' (~100 pc); central position fixed to 2D Gaussian centroid
assumptions: Rotating thin disk geometry with scale height 0.01'' (~100 pc)

recipe.goal: Model kinematics with a thin rotating exponential disk to derive extended dynamical masses and half-light radii
recipe.method: Fit intensity and velocity maps with a thin rotating exponential disk model convolved with the synthesized beam, using emcee MCMC to sample free parameters and derive the dynamical mass enclosed within 10 kpc.
key_parameters: Free parameters: disk centre coordinates, half-light radius R_1/2 = 1.67 * R_d, inclination, position angle, dynamical mass (enclosed within 10 kpc), systemic velocity
assumptions: Exponential surface brightness profile Sigma proportional to e^(-r/R_d); mass surface density follows gas emission profile; circular velocity from Eq. 2.157 of Binney & Tremaine (2008); mass within 10 kpc represents total baryonic mass in disk

recipe.goal: Estimate dynamical masses of the J2315 merging system and its individual components
recipe.method: Calculate total mass using the virial theorem from projected separation and velocity difference, and calculate individual galaxy dynamical masses using the rotating disk estimator of Neri et al. (2003) with inclination angles from minor-to-major axis ratios.
key_parameters: Projected separation = 15 kpc, velocity separation = 170 km/s; inclinations = 52 deg (QSO host) and 61 deg (northern companion)
assumptions: Virial theorem with galaxies moving along the line-of-sight; or individual rotating disks with inclination = arccos(minor/major axis ratio)

recipe.goal: Derive stellar masses, molecular gas fractions, and revised black hole masses
recipe.method: Combine dynamical masses with gas masses from Paper I to infer stellar masses via M_* = M_dyn - M_gas - M_BH and gas fractions M_gas / M_*; re-derive black hole masses using the Bongiorno et al. (2014) relation from Halpha FWHM and 2-10 keV X-ray luminosity.
key_parameters: L_2-10keV = 1.1x10^45 erg/s (J1234) and 3.0x10^45 erg/s (J2315); gas masses from Paper I
assumptions: Disks are baryon-dominated out to 10 kpc; M_* = M_dyn - M_gas - M_BH

recipe.goal: Compare M_BH-M_gal relation with Illustris simulations and track evolutionary slopes
recipe.method: Place J1234 and J2315 on the M_BH-M_gal plane alongside z ~ 4-6 quasars and Illustris z ~ 2 galaxies, and compute the mean evolutionary slope alpha in the log(M_BH)-log(M_*) plane for the 10 most massive black holes in Illustris from z = 6 to z = 2.5 and from z = 2.5 to z = 0.5.
key_parameters: 10 most massive black holes in Illustris-1 at z1 = 2.5 (tracked to z2 = 0.5) and at z1 = 6 (tracked to z2 = 2.5)
assumptions: Flat LambdaCDM cosmology with H0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_M = 0.3, Omega_Lambda = 0.7
